title.med: FLAIR: T2 with the water nulled

summary.undergrad: [[flair|FLAIR]] (pane B) is a T2 image with one change: the signal from free fluid is switched off, so the ventricles turn dark while the brain tissue keeps its T2 look. Pane A is the main view and pane B the second one; the cursor is linked, so both always show the same spot.
summary.med: FLAIR adds an inversion pulse timed to null free water, so CSF is dark while the remaining contrast stays T2-weighted. Tissue with increased water content therefore stays bright next to dark CSF, which makes FLAIR sensitive to periventricular and cortical changes. Pane A is the main view and pane B the second one; the cursor is linked, so both always show the same spot.

text.undergrad: Bright on T2 (A), dark on FLAIR (B). That is the whole trick of FLAIR.
text.med: CSF: hyperintense on T2, nulled (hypointense) on FLAIR by the inversion time.

text.undergrad: Brain tissue looks similar on both, because FLAIR keeps the T2 contrast of tissue.
text.med: Normal white matter is mildly hypointense to cortex on both T2 and FLAIR.

text.undergrad: The fluid inside the eye is free water too, so it is also darkened on FLAIR.
text.med: Vitreous is free water and is largely suppressed on FLAIR, like CSF.
